To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the nucleon polarizabilities can be explained by a model with a pion cloud surrounding the quark degrees of freedoms.
the pion cloud plays an essential role for a consistent description of the nucleon form factors.
the nucleon form factors can be well explained by the pion cloud, but only in the CDM.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the role of the pion cloud in the nucleon and we have shown that the electric and magnetic dipole polarizabilities as well as different form factors as obtained in pion electro-production are particularly sensitive to this cloud.

the calculation of the pion cloud contributions to the nucleon properties in the LSM and CDM.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pion cloud plays an important role in the nucleon, but the details of its contribution to various properties depend strongly on the model assumptions.
the pion cloud in baryons is not negligible but also not as important as in the LSM.
a model which includes a pion cloud is needed to describe the pion electroproduction data, but that the LSM is ruled out.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the LSM predicts too strong a pion cloud and that the CDM is a good candidate to describe the nucleon properties. [1]
the LSM is too simple to explain the nucleon properties, while the CDM is a reasonable model.
we can explain the electric polarizability and the magnetic polarizability with the LSM and the chiral CDM.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pion cloud is important for many observables and that it cannot be neglected.
the polarizability is a very good indicator of the size of the pion cloud in a baryon, and that a large polarizability can be used to constrain the size of the meson cloud in the nucleon.
the CDM is a much better model for the pion cloud in nucleons than the LSM. [1]
